title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Building a project whose [MessagePackObject] type has a member typed as a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (for example a ValueTuple-like or a custom generic struct in another project or package) finishes without the source generator throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.
The same holds when the referenced generic value type is a record struct.
No CS8785-style warning saying the generator failed shows up for these member types.
expectedTests: A generator snapshot test compiles a referenced assembly that defines a generic struct, references it from a [MessagePackObject] type with a closed-generic member, and checks that generation finishes with no exception and no generator diagnostics.
A matching snapshot test does the same with a generic record struct from a referenced assembly.

expectedBehaviours: Running the MessagePack analyzers on a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly does not throw, and no AD0001 analyzer-exception warning is reported.
The analyzer reports only the diagnostics that apply. The member type alone produces no spurious MsgPack diagnostics.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a metadata reference to an assembly that defines a generic struct expects no diagnostics and no analyzer exception for a [MessagePackObject] member of that closed generic type.

expectedBehaviours: The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver and a formatter for the [MessagePackObject] type, just as it does when the generic struct is declared in the same project.
At runtime the type can be serialized and deserialized through the generated resolver, and the closed-generic member round-trips.
expectedTests: A snapshot test checks that the generated sources for the cross-assembly closed-generic-struct case include the resolver and formatter, saved as expected output files under Resources.
A runtime or integration test round-trips an instance whose member is a closed generic struct from another assembly using the generated resolver.

expectedBehaviours: For these inputs the build output contains no warning saying the generator or analyzer threw an exception, so the assembly cannot quietly end up without a resolver.
If the generator cannot handle a member type, it says so with a meaningful diagnostic or a failed build. It does not silently skip resolver generation.
expectedTests: A test checks that the generator run result for the reproduction case has no exception and no generator-failure warnings, and that the generated resolver source is present.

expectedBehaviours: Existing generator snapshot outputs for generic classes, non-generic structs and generic types declared in the same project stay the same.
Existing analyzer tests keep passing, with the same diagnostics for these existing cases.
expectedTests: The existing snapshot test suite passes and no expected output files under Resources change for unrelated cases.
Snapshot tests cover a same-project generic struct and a referenced-assembly generic class, and confirm the output is the same as before.

story.what: TypeCollector no longer indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] when building member diagnostics. A property's key-null diagnostic now gets its location from a new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper, and a field's MemberNeedsKey diagnostic uses FirstOrDefault(). Both return null for symbols that come from metadata. The analyzer's report callback is also wrapped so that diagnostics whose location is not a source tree of the current compilation are dropped. New tests compile a generic struct or record struct into a metadata-only assembly, use a closed instance of it as a member, and check that the build has no diagnostics and that the resolver is generated.
story.why: MP-2283: a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly has members that exist only in metadata. Indexing their empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences threw IndexOutOfRangeException in both the generator and the analyzer, and the assembly ended up without its generated resolver. Reporting a diagnostic at a location outside the compilation is also not allowed for analyzers. The README and MsgPack004 docs now say that such members are diagnosed by the project that defines them.

touches.note: Wraps the non-null analyzer report callback with ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. Stays null in generator mode.
BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (property) and MemberNeedsKey (field) diagnostics now resolve their location null-safely.
New helper. Returns the property identifier location, or null when the property has no source declaration.
New helper. Forwards a diagnostic only if its location is in source and its tree belongs to this compilation.
New helper that compiles the defining source to an image, runs the verifier on the usage source and checks the generated resolver hint name.
Three new facts: a generic struct, a generic record struct, and a generic struct with an unkeyed member, each from a metadata reference.

claims.text: When a keyed property has neither an int nor a string key, the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic used to cast DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]. It now gets its location from GetPropertyIdentifierLocation, which uses FirstOrDefault() and a safe 'as' cast, so a property that exists only in metadata gives a null location instead of throwing.

findings.detail: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation has no fallback to the containing type. When the property has no source declaration it returns null.
findings.statement: The new helper falls back to the location of the containing type when the property has no source declaration.
